prompt: For an actual six-element array, classify the pointer at index 6. Choose whether it can be formed and whether it can be dereferenced as an element.

model.operation: form samples + 6, then consider dereferencing it

feedback.correct: The one-past pointer may mark the array boundary, but it does not point to a readable element.

incorrect.cannot_form: C permits forming the one-past pointer for an actual array; forming it is different from reading through it.
incorrect.can_read_one_past: The one-past position is not an element. Do not evaluate a dereference there.
incorrect.wrong_boundary: Six elements have indices 0 through 5. The position after them has index 6.
incorrect.other: Classify pointer formation and element access as two separate operations.

hints.text: Separate making a pointer value from accessing an element through it.
For six elements, index 5 is last and index 6 is the boundary after it.
The one-past pointer may be formed, but it may not be dereferenced.

citations.claim: The one-past pointer may be formed but cannot be used as an array element.
Array subscripting is defined through pointer addition and indirection; the one-past restriction follows from the cited pointer-arithmetic clause.
